newsitem.title: UK: Liberty Intl money market fund taps growing trend.
newsitem.headline: Liberty Intl money market fund taps growing trend.

text.p: Liberty International Holdings has launched a two-class money market fund which it says is tapping a growing trend towards professional money management by European institutions.

Liberty CEO Ron Mitchell said in an interview that money market funds were well established instruments in the U.S. (where the market amounts to over $750 billion) but are not so familiar to European markets as yet.

"We are responding to a trend where major corporations and banks are borrowing more from the market place and top banks are attracting more money than they require. Cash is complex to manage and it is often easier and cheaper to outsource it."
"Also, with leading stock markets at record highs there is a growing trend to cash investment and the problem of uncompetitive deposit rates is compounded," he said.
The fund, AAA-M rated by Standard & Poors, will start with dollar and sterling classes, actively managed from Jersey by Liberty International.

There are no initial charges and the annual management fee of 0.25 percent has been discounted by 50 percent until the year end. With a minimum investment if 100,000 stg or $150,000 the fund is aimed at high net worth individuals or institutions.
"Around $600 billion flows through the offshore centres -- Jersey, Guernsey and Isle of Man every year. Half of that is through bank deposits. This is what we are targeting," said Mitchell.
He said Liberty would be putting in $100 million and 100 million stg to start off the two funds "so that we can get wholesale money market rates straight away."

The funds are also likely to be boosted by business from Liberty's onshore sister company Hermes Liberty International Pensions Ltd, the result of a recent alliance with Hermes Investment Management, which handles the 1.5 billion stg BT Pension Scheme.
Mitchell said cash holdings from the new venture could be managed by Liberty International offshore, and more UK pension business would be sought.

As an umbrella fund, the new money market structure will also be able to add sub-classes if necessary. "For example if EMU (Ecominic and Monetary Union) gets going, it would be no problem for us to add a Euro fund," Mitchell noted.
Most of the investment will be in A1-plus paper with a small component in A1 paper with an average maturity of 60 days. No more than 10 percent of the fund can be held to any counterparty.

The sterling fund is aiming to offer an average three month return of 5.75 percent, annualised and net of fees, and the dollar fund 5.3 percent, against usual bank rates of 4.5 percent for sterling and 4.10 percent for dollar investments.

Liberty International Holdings plc is 69 percent held by South African life insurance company Liberty Life, the fourth largest company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, with funds under management of $23 billion.
